title: Hotpool orphaning after lease consolidation bug causing tenant capacity starvation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
A regression in the lease consolidation path within the reserved-pool allocator caused a class of allocations (recently consolidated leases) to be marked as 'inactive' for hotpool rebalancing. The result: hotpool nodes that should have been available for tenant burst allocations were effectively orphaned — they remained assigned but invisible to the autoscaler admission logic. Symptoms appeared as intermittent tenant throttles, sudden failure to honor burst credits, and frequent reserved-pool headroom reports showing 'available' slots that the admission controller could not bind to live requests.

Scope & customer impact:
- Reproduced in staging and observed correlated customer escalations on Dedicated over the last 48h.
- Affected tenants experienced increased 429s during microbursts and an inability to leverage burst credits even though metrics reported free headroom.
- Customer escalations: 3 enterprise customers reported degraded SLA and one opened an urgent contract-level escalation.

Root cause (high level):
- A recent change in lease consolidation (merge_small_leases_v2) added a fast-path that clears a transient 'active' flag while merging metadata. Due to a race between lease consolidation finalization and the hotpool refresh routine, some nodes' lease records end up with consolidated metadata but without the expected index entries used by the autoscaler admission cache. The admission cache therefore skipped those nodes when computing available hot slots.

Immediate mitigation/workaround applied:
- Short-term hotfix: disabled merge_small_leases_v2 in the running coordinator (hot patch) which restored consistent admission behavior within 12 minutes for most regions.
- Runbook action: forced a hotpool refresh and full admission cache rebuild in the affected AZs. This recovered ~85% of orphaned nodes within 30 minutes.
- Customer comms: Sent targeted updates to the three affected customers explaining the mitigation and ETA for a permanent fix.

Longer-term fix plan:
1) Patch: Add atomic commit to lease consolidation so the 'active' flag is only cleared after index entries are inserted. Implement write-ahead marker for consolidation operations. (PR: linked in comments below)
2) Hardening: Add admission cache self-heal that detects inconsistent node index count vs lease metadata and triggers a reconciliation job.
3) Observability: Add new telemetry for consolidation events, cache miss rates keyed by zone, and orphan-detection alerting (SLO delta > 5% over 5m).
4) E2E test: Add flaky/regression test that simulates consolidation + concurrent admission refresh to catch race.

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Patch merged and deployed to canary, with no regressions observed in automated canary workloads.
- Admission cache reconciliation job prevents recurrence in canary for 48h.
- Postmortem and incident summary published to #incidents and customers updated.

Notes on risk and rollout:
- Patch touches allocation and consolidation critical path; default rollout path: canary -> regional canary -> global. We will keep merge_small_leases_v2 disabled on prod until canary shows stability.
- If the reconciliation job is noisy, we will gate it behind a feature flag for gradual ramp.
